construction.note: This was developed by extending Tastir’s simpler eight-fold rosette to sixteen divisions. The creation commit describes that generalisation; no published sequence is credited.
construction.changes: It is a construction study, not a reconstruction of the Bou Inania wall. The photographed Bou Inania rosette used in the early comparison was later identified as twelve-fold, and its surrounding network differs substantially.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the unit for every length.

steps.text: Draw a circle with centre O through A. Its radius is the unit for the whole pattern.
Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at E, N, W and S. These letters stand for east, north, west and south.
Draw the lines through O that halve the angles at O between E and N, and between N and W. These lines cross the circle at NE, NW, SW and SE.
Draw a vertical line through each of E and W. Draw a horizontal line through each of N and S. These lines make a square with corners J, K, L and M. Join J, K, L and M to mark the tile that repeats.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a vertical line through each of E and W. Draw a horizontal line through N. Join J, K, L and M to mark the square tile that repeats. Its bottom side is not needed as a line.

steps.text: Draw the lines through O that halve the four angles between E, NE, N, NW and W. The first crosses the circle at R. Turn R round O by 45°, seven times. The circle is now cut into sixteen.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw the line through O that halves the angle at O between E and NE. It crosses the circle at R. Turn R round O by 45°, seven times. The circle is now cut into sixteen.

steps.text: Draw a line through R, at 90° to the line from O to R. It crosses the vertical line through E at T, a corner of the sixteen-sided figure round the rosette.
Draw a straight line through O and T. Draw a circle with centre T through E. It crosses the line from O to T at C. Turn this circle and C round O by 22.5°, fifteen times.
Draw a straight line through C and the copy of C seven places round, counter-clockwise. Turn this line round O by 22.5°, fifteen times. The sixteen lines make the star at the heart of the rosette.

Draw two lines through E, parallel to the lines from O to the fourth and fifth copies of C. Turn these two lines round O by 22.5°, fifteen times. Where they cross the star lines, they turn into petals.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw two lines through E, sloping like the lines from O to the fourth and fifth copies of C. Turn these two lines round O by 22.5°, fifteen times. Where they cross the star lines, they turn into petals.

steps.text: Mark G, where the upper line through E crosses a star line. Mark P, where that star line crosses the line from O to R. Mark H and Q in the same way below. Turn G, P, H and Q round O by 22.5°, fifteen times.

ink.text: Ink each petal from the circle to a point of the star. Sixteen petals ring a sixteen-pointed star.

parts.text: Ink from E through G to P. Ink from E through H to Q. These lines make one petal.
Ink the same two lines at each of the other fifteen points on the circle. Tick “Also ink the copies round the centre” to ink them all at once.

pattern.text: Put copies of the tile side by side. Each rosette touches its four neighbours at the tips of its petals. The ground between them is one piece.

expect.note: Golden values, in units of OA, computed by the engine and checked for sixteen-fold symmetry, no slivers, and pieces that exactly fill the tile.
